chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from Abu al-Hasan (the preceding one), peace be upon him, who said:
The divorce of a female slave is two revocations, and her waiting period is two menstruations; if she has ceased menstruating, then her waiting period is one month and a half.
ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period and divorce procedure for a female slave in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), establishing the distinct legal status of a female slave (ama) in divorce, where her iddah is defined by two menstruations rather than three, reflecting the Qur'anic principle of halving obligations for slaves. This narration highlights the practical application of iddah rules in classical Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing between menstruating and menopausal slaves to ensure precise calculation of the waiting period.
